Playbook.name: Windows — Event Log Cleared (All Channels) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A Windows event log was cleared - Security (1102) or System/Application (104) - across channels, excluding the known benign hq-adsync-app-p Application clear. Triage question: anti-forensic evidence destruction, or sanctioned maintenance?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Clearing event logs removes local evidence of intrusion activity; doing it across channels is a strong post-exploitation signal.

LogSources.LogSource: Windows Security/System/Application logs - logs-system.security-*, logs-system.system-*, logs-system.application-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the log clear is anti-forensic evidence destruction or sanctioned maintenance.

Step.name: Which channels were cleared, by whom, and on how many hosts
Step.Purpose: Multiple channels/hosts cleared close together is broad anti-forensics; a single maintenance clear differs.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-*,logs-system.system-*,logs-system.application-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1102","104") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, host.name, event.code, winlog.channel, winlog.event_data.SubjectUserName | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 30
Step.AnalystNotes: Security(1102) + System/Application(104) cleared on one host in minutes = anti-forensics. Isolated Application 104 on a known host = benign service behavior.

Step.name: Preceding suspicious activity on the host
Step.Purpose: Suspicious privileged activity just before the clear is what the actor is erasing.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.code IN ("4624","4672","4688","7045","4720") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code), users = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName) BY winlog.event_data.LogonType | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: New privileged logon + service install before the clear = intrusion sequence. Quiet history = maintenance.

Node.Condition: Multiple channels/hosts cleared, or suspicious activity precedes the clear.
Non-admin or unexpected principal clearing a production host with no maintenance record.
Known admin clearing during a documented maintenance/reimage.
Admin clear, no ticket, quiet history.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-CLEARALL-EVENT, INV-02-CLEARALL-PRECEDING to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Preserve SIEM copies; isolate the host; reconstruct from forwarded logs; open IR.
Fix the job; ensure forwarding precedes any clear.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
